name: adversarial-inputs-v1
comment: Malformed and hostile inputs shared by the Java, Go, .NET and Android test suites. One implementation rejecting an input does not mean the input is handled: an attacker picks whichever node runs the most permissive implementation, so these run everywhere. expect=reject means the decoder must refuse. expect=parse-or-reject means either answer is correct but an unhandled exception, a crash, or a half-built object the caller then trusts is not. No case may take longer than a few milliseconds to decide.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: A zero-length datagram is what a closed socket or a stripped packet produces.

cases.name: magic-only
cases.why: The magic alone carries no header; accepting it would read past the buffer.

cases.name: truncated-header
cases.why: A header cut mid-field is what a path MTU drop produces.

cases.name: magic-in-turn-channeldata-range
cases.why: SPM2 magic opens with 0x5350, inside the TURN ChannelData range 0x4000-0x7fff. Demultiplexing must decide by whether the parse succeeds, not by the range; deciding by range alone made the Go client claim and then drop every direct data frame.

cases.name: turn-channeldata-valid-shape
cases.why: A well-formed ChannelData frame must not be mistaken for a data frame either.

cases.name: turn-channeldata-length-overrun
cases.why: A declared length far beyond the datagram is the classic length-field attack.

cases.name: all-zero-64
cases.why: Zeros hit any code that treats a zero length or zero epoch as a sentinel.

cases.name: all-ones-64
cases.why: 0xFF fills exercise signed/unsigned confusion and maximum-value length fields.

cases.name: ascii-json-fragment
cases.why: A JSON fragment reaches decoders that sniff for a leading brace.

cases.name: stun-magic-cookie-only
cases.why: A STUN header truncated right after the magic cookie, with no transaction id.

cases.name: stun-attribute-length-overrun
cases.why: An attribute claiming more bytes than the message holds.
